source.title: Kontsevich Graphs Act on Nambu-Poisson Brackets, VI. Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Can one find a Poisson bracket P on an affine manifold and a nontrivial Kontsevich graph cocycle action whose induced infinitesimal deformation changes P in a way that is not merely a coordinate change along a vector field, thereby producing a family of inequivalent Poisson structures?

evidence.quote: It remains an open problem to find an example of nontrivial graph cocycle action on a Poisson bracket, thus spreading it to a family of inequivalent structures not related by a coordinate change.
Beyond the tetrahedron γ3, there are countably many ‘good’ nontrivial graph cocycles: γ5, γ7, . . .

accepted.question_text: For Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets on R^d of the form {f, g}_d(x) = rho(x) det(partial(f, g, a_1, ..., a_{d-2}) / partial(x_1, ..., x_d)), where the functions a_i are Casimirs satisfying {f, a_i}_d = 0, does Kontsevich's tetrahedral graph cocycle gamma_3 act nontrivially on the space of such Nambu-Poisson brackets in dimensions d >= 3, or is every resulting gamma_3-flow only a coordinate-change coboundary generated by a vector field?

evidence.quote: we explore the open problem of (non)triviality for Kontsevich’s tetrahedral graph cocycle action on the space of Nambu–Poisson brackets.
was introduced in [1]; its Casimirs ai ∈ C 1 (Rd ) satisfy {f, ai }d ≡ 0.
Recall the standard problem in deformation theory: is the γ3-flow nontrivial, i.e. does the change of Poisson bivector not amount to a change of coordinates along a vector field

accepted.question_text: Assume that the tetrahedral Kontsevich graph flow on a Nambu-Poisson bracket in dimension d + 1 is trivial, so that Q_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P tensor 4) can be written as the Poisson coboundary [[P, X_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P tensor 3)]]. Is the trivializing vector field X_{gamma_3}^{d+1} always expressible as a linear combination of the (d + 1)-dimensional descendants of the two-dimensional sunflower graph X_{gamma_3} = (0, 1; 1, 3; 1, 2) + 2(0, 2; 1, 3; 1, 2), where descendants are produced in the dimensional step by adjoining the new Casimir and applying the stated Leibniz-rule expansion?

evidence.quote: then is X~ γ3 d+1 found over linear combinations of the ‘sunflower’ descendants from 2D ?
Every expansion of Leibniz rule thus yields a linear combination of (d+1)-dimensional Nambu micro-graph descendants of the originally taken d-dimensional Nambu micro-graph.

accepted.question_text: If the sunflower-descendant ansatz for the dimension d + 1 trivializing vector field X_{gamma_3}^{d+1} is valid, is it sufficient to search only over the union of two families: the (d + 1)-descendants of the known dimension-d solution X_{gamma_3}^d and the (d + 1)-descendants of vanishing one-vector Nambu micro-graphs over R^d?

evidence.quote: If yes, is X~ γ3 d+1 found over the union of (d + 1)-descendants for the underlying solution X~ γ3 d and vanishing 1-vector micro-graphs over Rd ?
to find X~ γ3 d>2 for the Nambu class, we use micro-graphs on m = 1 sink and n = 3 copies of bracket (1) over Rd.

accepted.question_text: For the vanishing one-vector Nambu micro-graphs that are needed in the dimensional shift d -> d + 1, do all indispensable examples come from descendants of an underlying vanishing set already present over R^{d-1}, rather than from new vanishing micro-graphs whose vanishing mechanisms first appear in the higher dimension?

evidence.quote: Do these indispensable (cf. [6]) vanishing micro-graphs stem only from the underlying vanishing set in Rd−1 through their descendants ?
there appear no new (starting to work) mechanisms of φ(Γd+1) = 0 w.r.t. φ(Γd) = 0.

accepted.question_text: What group-theoretic and topological mechanism makes Nambu micro-graphs and their linear combinations vanish as differential-polynomial formulas, especially in cases where a vanishing micro-graph has trivial automorphism group and no evident symmetry that marks the cancelling factors?

evidence.quote: What is the group-theoretic and topological mechanism of vanishing for Nambu micro-graphs and their linear combinations ?
To reveal this mechanism in full is a standing problem; the impact of topology (in Γ) on arithmetic (in φ(Γ)) will make possible the study of d ≳ 5, so far costly.
